title: Sequence-aware phase-gates for session-coherent model promotes
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: We observed intermittent regressions when promoting sequence-sensitive models because session affinity and temporal ordering were not respected during gradual promotes. This PR introduces a lightweight phase-gate controller that enforces session-coherent promotes: a promote can only advance past a gate when sampled session cohorts have completed a verification window. The controller is sequence-aware (tracks session_id and sequence offsets) and integrates with existing telemetry gates to avoid split-brain behavior between short-lived sessions and long-running conversations.

Summary of changes: Adds a new PhaseGate controller, a small runtime token used to bind sessions to a promote phase (temporal affinity token), rehearsal-only dry-run logic for simulated promotes, and a rollback escrow mechanism that snapshots in-flight KV/segment pointers to allow deterministic rewind for affected sessions. The implementation is intentionally incremental: the controller runs as an opt-in mode for rollout definitions and uses existing metrics gates for SLO checks.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc (linked) and sequence diagrams included in docs/rollouts/sequence-aware.md
- [x] PhaseGate controller and reconciliation loop implemented in pkg/rollout/controller.go
- [x] Dry-run rehearsal harness added (internal/sim/rehearsal_runner.go) and integrated with CI smoke tests
- [x] UI for configuring temporal windows and holdpoints (web/ui/rollout-editor.tsx)
- [x] E2E spec and integration tests (tests/integration/phasegate_smoke_test.go)
- [x] Chart templates for private/dedicated deployments updated (charts/redwood-rollout/templates/phase-gate.yaml)

Design notes: The PhaseGate concept is a finite-state gate per-rollout that moves through {Open, Hold, Verify, Commit, Rewind}. Gates are evaluated over a sliding verification window (configurable, default 5m) and compute metrics over session-cohorts rather than raw request-level aggregates. This avoids false positives from bursty short-lived traffic.

Temporal affinity token: When a session's first request enters a promoted bucket, we attach a short-lived affinity token that pins that session to a phase until the session exceeds a configured grace offset or the gate transitions to Commit. Tokens are small (opaque 64-bit) and expire; they are stored in the runtime KV cache index and in a replay-safe snapshot for rollback.

Rollback escrow: To allow deterministic rewinds for sessions pinned to promoted paths, we snapshot per-session KV pointers into a rollback escrow object when the gate crosses Verify. If a gate transitions to Rewind (triggered by gate-level SLO failure or manual backout), the controller replays session handoffs using the escrow to restore prior KV pointers and route new requests to the previous variant until sessions drain. The escrow payload is intentionally compact (pointers, not full state).

Metrics gates and thresholds used in tests: the default verification gate requires: p50 latency <= baseline * 1.10; 99th latency increase < 1.25x; error-rate delta <= 0.1% absolute; semantic-regression score (customer-defined eval) not degraded. All thresholds are configurable per-rollout.

Testing and rollout plan: We ran the following checks locally and in staging: unit tests for controller reconciliation, integration smoke that replays synthetic session traces through the rehearser, and a staged deploy to a single dedicated cluster with canary fraction 1%. After two days of warm traffic the gate was promoted to 10% and held for the default verification window. CI had one flaky test on first run (integration timeout) — rerun passed.

Backward compatibility and opt-in: The controller is opt-in via a new field in rollout spec: sequencePhase: {enabled: true, verificationWindow: "5m", sessionGrace: "30s"}. Existing rollouts without this field are unaffected.

Operational notes: Operators should monitor: rollout.phase_gate.duration, rollout.session_pinned_count, rollback_escrow.size, and gate_verification.failures. A new quick-run diagnostic (redwood rollout inspect --phase-gate) was added to surface live tokens and escrow snapshots for debugging.

Follow-ups: 1) Add a confetti-free audit trail hook to the Console (UX ticket PM-412) that shows per-session promote decisions. 2) Extend rehearsal harness to replay real production traces (privacy opt-in), tracked in ENG-1968.

Related: references ENG-1894 design ticket; SUP-2210 for a customer incident that motivated the session-coherent requirement.

Full description and design diagrams available in docs/rollouts/sequence-aware.md

review_comments: Elliot Park: Nice incremental approach. Please add a short-lived counter to ensure token churn doesn't spike KV index pressure. Also request a small table in the docs showing default thresholds vs. recommended tight thresholds.
Ava Chen: Added token_gc counter and a retention strategy in escrow; expanded docs with thresholds table. See docs changes.
Sofia Martinez: Integration tests look good. I'm concerned about the performance impact when many long-lived sessions are pinned. Can we add a backpressure knob to avoid O(N) reconciliation?

Ava Chen: Added session_pinned_limit and background compaction path; controller will sample when pinned sessions exceed threshold. Added a longitudinal test in tests/integration/phasegate_smoke_test.go to validate sampling behavior.
Jonas Klein: Approved after CI green and minor nits fixed (typo in docs).
ci_checks: ci/integration — fail (timeout on first run), rerun — pass
testing_summary: Unit coverage + integration smoke runs. Rehearsal runner simulates 10k synthetic sessions with 7% long-lived distribution; validated rollback escrow restores session routes deterministically. Performance impact measured on staging: <2.3% memory delta for KV index at 10% promote in heavy session workloads. Added a mitigation knob session_pinned_limit to cap reconciliation work.
release_notes: Add opt-in sequence-aware PhaseGate controller for session-coherent model promotes. Enables temporal affinity tokens and rollback escrow to offer deterministic rewinds for pinned sessions. Opt-in via rollout spec field 'sequencePhase'.
notes_for_oncall: If a gate is stuck in Hold beyond verificationWindow: check rollout.phase_gate.duration and rollback_escrow.size, then run 'redwood rollout inspect --phase-gate' to see pinned token counts. Manual backout available via 'redwood rollout promote --force-rewind'.
